extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedures, and sanctions for USPTO disciplinary proceedings resolving allegations of professional misconduct by persons who practice before the Office, including jurisdictional bases, applicable professional conduct rules, specified sanctions, and the process for probationary enforcement and publication of orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.  Respondent has practiced before the Office in trademark matters and is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory and regulatory bases for USPTO disciplinary authority over persons who practice before the Office (citations provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of professional conduct rules by date of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective May 3, 2013, the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.01–11.901) apply to persons who practice before the Office.  Since the alleged conduct occurred prior to May 3, 2013, the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112) is applicable in this case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which version of the USPTO ethical rules governs based on the date of the alleged misconduct; cite appropriate regulatory sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited conduct: prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, based on the stipulated facts, he violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) by engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) as the regulatory basis for disciplining conduct that undermines the administration of justice (examples here include failing to comply with court discovery orders and filing misleading or improper statements in briefs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: public reprimand and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement orders that Respondent is publicly reprimanded and shall serve a one year probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reprimand and probation are available sanctions; the Final Order explicitly imposes both in this settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional continued practice during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be permitted to practice trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO during his probationary period unless his probation is revoked and he is suspended by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation does not automatically bar practice in non-patent matters before the Office unless further action is taken to suspend or exclude the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and initial enforcement step
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Agreement, Final Order, or any Disciplinary Rule during the probationary period, the OED Director shall issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order that Respondent be immediately suspended for up to sixty (60) days for the violation set forth in paragraph 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause is the first enforcement mechanism used by OED when noncompliance is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Order to Show Cause and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order to Show Cause shall be sent to Respondent at the last address of record Respondent furnished to the California State Bar Association; Respondent shall be granted fifteen (15) calendar days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies method of service (address of record with state bar) and a fixed 15-calendar-day response period for the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director for suspension request
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day period and consideration of any response, the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director or his designee: (A) the Order to Show Cause, (B) Respondent's response to the Order to Show Cause, if any, and (C) argument and evidence causing the OED Director to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, and request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend Respondent for up to sixty (60) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the materials and arguments OED must forward to the USPTO Director to obtain an immediate suspension of up to 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: No stay of suspension pending review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the referral and Respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any such review of the suspension shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any review process does not automatically stay or delay an imposed suspension; suspension takes immediate effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (publicly accessible through the Office's website) and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the reprimand and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary Final Orders are published electronically and in the Official Gazette; the notice includes factual summary and reminders to practitioners of duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Official Gazette notice and practitioner reminder
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice states the practitioner's name and location, that he is not a registered patent practitioner, that he has been publicly reprimanded and placed on probation for one year, summarizes the misconduct (e.g., failing to comply with court discovery orders; making misleading and improper statements), and reminds practitioners of their duty to fully comply with court orders and be honest and candid in all documents filed with any court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the Official Gazette notice both to inform the public and to remind practitioners of professional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (i) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (ii) in any future disciplinary proceeding (A) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (B) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used subsequently as aggravation or rebuttal; settlement does not preclude future consideration of the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative closing of pending USPTO disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall file a joint motion dismissing the USPTO disciplinary proceeding pending against Respondent within fourteen days after entry of any Final Order approving this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following approval of the settlement and Final Order, the parties are to move to dismiss the pending disciplinary matter within 14 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order approving this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement specifies that each side pays its own costs (no indication of payment of costs by respondent to the Office).
